All lane and ramp closures are subject to the approval of the Region traffic engineer. When the work zone is not active the traffic control drums must be placed completely within the closed lane to accommodate OSOW vehicles. CTH JG will be closed while the wing wall, bearings and north abutment expansion joint are replaced at B-13-300 (CTH JG over USH 18). Interim liquidated damages will be accessed if the STH 78 and CTH ID detours or the CTH JG closure exceeds the maximum calendars days shown in the special provisions. The STH 78 and CTH ID detours will not be allowed to occur at the same time. Closure of CTH JG is not permitted while the STH 78 or CTH ID detours are in place. #### **How was the work zone capacity determined?**

STH 32 has a 2017 AADT of 13,000. The WisDOT planning-level forecasts do not show any traffic growth at this location, so for the purpose of this analysis a 2% annual growth rate was used. The construction year (2021) AADT would be approximately 14,000. This corridor has a Seasonal Factor Group (SFG) 2 for Urban Other. This results in a K30 value of 0.12 and a directional distribution of 59/41. The peak hour directional volume along STH 32 is estimated to be 990 vph. There is not expected to be any capacity issues along this portion of STH 32 since capacity of a single lane is expected to be higher than 1,000 vphpl. Capacity will be reduced even further at the STH 32 & STH 11 intersection due to closing one lane of the EB left turn movement and one NB thru lane. Synchro 11 and SimTraffic traffic modeling software, using Highway Capacity Manual (HCM) 6th Edition methodology, was used to estimate traffic conditions during these closures. Project ID 7650-00-04/74: The spot improvement project consists of replacing Culvert C-47-719 under STH 29 just south of 805th Avenue with a two-cell concrete box culvert B-47-0230. Due to the depth of the culvert, it is required to reconstruct the roadway for approximately 70' feet north and south of the culvert, install new guardrail along both sides of the roadway, and reconstruct the multi-use trail along the east side of the roadway. The existing safety rail along the multi-use trail will be salvaged and replaced. The reconstructed roadway will include a 7-inch asphaltic pavement over base aggregate and will maintain 12-foot travel lanes but will provide a wider 5-foot paved shoulder and 3-foot gravel shoulder. Centerline and shoulder rumble strips will be constructed. All new pavement marking will be installed as well. Project ID 7650-01-05/75: The pavement replacement project along STH 29 includes replacing the existing 7-inch concrete pavement with new 7-inch asphaltic pavement. The 12-foot travel lanes will be maintained, as well as the overall shoulder width of 8 feet; however, the paved shoulder will be widened to 5 feet. Both the roadway cross slope and the superelevation of the curve just south of the STH 29 and 690th Street intersection will be adjusted to current design standards. The existing bypass lane for westbound

STH 29 traffic at CTH E will be removed and a dedicated left turn lane will be provided. The curb and gutter in the southeast quadrant of the STH 29 and Cemetery Road intersection will be redesigned to accommodate large truck turning movements. Centerline and shoulder rumble strips will be constructed. One culvert along the project limits will be replaced and another two culverts will be extended; all other existing culverts will remain. All existing guardrail within the project limits will be replaced. All new pavement marking will be installed as well. The project also includes rehabilitating the bridge B-47-21 over Greenwood Valley Creek. The top 1.5 inches of the existing bridge deck will be removed and replaced with a new 1.5-inch concrete surface. The bridge deck will be widened 8 inches and new, crash-worthy bridge railing will be installed. Guardrail will be replaced in all quadrants of the bridge approach. New concrete pavement approach slabs will be constructed north and south of the existing bridge. All rebar that has been exposed will be properly cleaned and sealed to maintain its structural integrity. Maintenance of the superstructure will be completed. Project ID 7650-02-03/73: The HSIP project includes reconfiguring the STH 29 and CTH FF intersection to provide dedicated left turn lanes for westbound and eastbound STH 29 traffic, a dedicated right turn lane for westbound STH 29 traffic, and reconfiguring the channelized right turn lane on the west leg of County FF. To reduce impacts to the multi-use trail and adjacent properties, the east side of the roadway edge will be maintained and widening of STH 29 will occur to the west. One existing culvert south of CTH FF will be extended. Shoulder rumble strips will be constructed. All new signs and pavement marking will be installed as well. ### **Briefly describe the staging planned for maintaining traffic:** Mainline I-94 will remain open to traffic throughout the project and work will be completed under staged construction. Staging plans are attached in this section. Single lane closures (reduced from 2-lanes to 1-lane) are permitted in each direction during overnight hours only (permitted closure times are identified in Section 6). The majority of work including pavement milling, base patching, and repaving operations will occur during the overnight hours when the lane closures are in place. Work not requiring lane closures may occur during daytime hours. See TMP ID 7551 for limited permitted daytime lane closure hours associated with the cable barrier work. Schedule/Sequencing of work and traffic control will be coordinated between the three tied let projects. Construction will include two general stages to avoid traffic control conflicts between the railroad bridge rehab and resurfacing projects (see description below). The cable barrier Segment 1 project is located within the resurfacing project limits and will be installed concurrently with the resurfacing work. Traffic control staging must be coordinated between these two projects. During overnight work, either separate work zones must be established for the cable barrier and resurfacing work with a minimum separation of 3 miles or a single work zone must be established encompassing both work activities that may not exceed 5 miles in length. Further, an inside lane closure for cable barrier work may not be preceded or followed by an outside lane closure for resurfacing work. The cable barrier Segment 2 limits are located more than 3 miles away from the CNW Railroad bridges (1067-01-85) and the resurfacing (1067-04-72) projects, allowing for separate work zone operations. However, the cable barrier Segment 2 is located in close proximity (less than 1 mile east) of a bridge re-decking/widening project along the County A overpass of I-94 (1067-02-72) which is scheduled to occur simultaneously in 2021. Overnight lane closures along I-94 are proposed with the County A overpass project. Due to the proximity of the work zones, lane closures with the cable barrier Segment 2 and County A overpass projects must be coordinated and any lane closures occurring simultaneously must be implemented to provide a single, continuous work zone. Overall project sequencing is summarized below. \*Stage 1 (May-July, 2021): -Complete westbound bridge rehab work. - Complete eastbound road resurfacing work. -Westbound road resurfacing work may occur with a minimum 3-mile separation maintained between the westbound bridge work. -Complete cable barrier Segment 1. Coordinate traffic control with resurfacing work (as discussed in previous paragraphs). -Complete cable barrier Segment 2. Single lane closures will be permitted in both directions. The maintenance crossover west of IH 41 will be closed off using type III barricades to prevent drivers from utilizing them during the STH 172/IH 41 ramp closures. A full closure will be required to complete the work along the single lane STH 172/IH 41 interchange ramps. Traffic will be detoured for the WB STH 172 ramp to SB IH 41 while the concrete pavement is being replaced. The detour will direct traffic along NB IH 41 to CTH VK (Lombardi Avenue). The work for the other single lane ramps will not have detours but lane closures will not be allowed between 6:00 am and 6:00 pm. #### **Describe how pedestrians will be accommodated during construction.** The curb ramps at the STH 172 & Packerland Drive/CTH EB intersection and STH 172/Babcock Road intersection will be replaced with the project. While the curb ramps are being replaced the associated sidewalk will be closed and appropriate signage will be in place. The public will be informed of the planned work and closure of the sidewalk through notifications to locals, press releases/media alerts, and through the 511 Traveler Information Website. The plan is to reach out to providers in the area prior to the closures that can help with transportation. This includes the ADRC, for people with disabilities, and local taxi service, for any other pedestrians. Notifications will be sent out to local municipalities, providers, and a press release about the closure and transportation options. This will get the word out about this work and get users to think ahead. The ADRC has a list of providers. Most are on-demand services. They can provide rides for all kinds of reasons. It is very possible that people with disabilities using these corridors have used these services before to get around town. People can call them directly and discuss transportation. If they use the route daily, then the transportation can be catered to their needs. This will depend on individual needs.
